raw_case_text:
The patient is a 38-year-old HIV + male, well controlled (CD4 count of 213 cells/mm3 with an undetectable viral load) on dolutegravir and emtricitabine-tenofovir, without any prior ocular problems. He presented with a nonulcerative papulonodular hypopigmented rash with lesions scattered along the bilateral upper and lower extremities, trunk, and abdomen [Figure 1]. H and E staining of the cutaneous biopsy showed Leishmaniasis chassis and infantum. Thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly were also noted. The patient immigrated to the US from Nicaragua at the age of 20 and he has remained in the US since his arrival. The patient was treated with intravenous amphotericin B liposome (7 of 9 doses) and then lost to follow-up. He presented a year later with the same papulonodular rash consistent with cutaneous leishmaniasis. He was retreated with amphotericin (14-dose course) and miltefosine for a 28-day course. Two days after stopping miltefosine, he developed progressive left eye redness, pain, and photophobia.
On day 7 of his symptoms, visual acuity declined to count fingers in the affected left eye. Biomicroscopy showed unilateral 3+ conjunctival and ciliary injections, corneal peripheral haze with focal areas of whitening without epithelial loss or ulceration, and 1+ anterior chamber cell [Figure 2]. No vitreoretinal involvement was noted; however, there was a shallow temporal choroidal effusion of the left eye. Anterior chamber paracentesis was performed for polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis for leishmaniasis. No corneal scrapings were performed since the epithelium was intact. Additional infectious workup included HZV aqueous PCR, serum RPR/FTA, QuantiFERON Gold, and serum VZV. All tests were found to be noncontributory. HIV monitoring laboratories revealed a rise in the HIV viral load to 10,500 copies/mL and a decline in CD4 count to 213 cells/mm3. No changes in medications or compliance were noted at that time.
Cautious initiation of topical steroid (prednisolone acetate 1%) every 2 h and cycloplegic (cyclopentolate 1%) three times per day was done under close monitoring and with the plan to change to topical amphotericin if any worsening occurred. The patient responded rapidly to the application of topical steroids with complete clearing of corneal infiltration and resolution of anterior uveitis [Figure 3]. The visual acuity returned to 20/20 by the Snellen chart. Ocular quiescence has remained off steroids for 2 years even though concurrent cutaneous and visceral disease did recur.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old HIV-positive male presented with progressive redness, pain, and photophobia in the left eye of 7 days duration.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, with a history of treated cutaneous and visceral lesions, presented with acute progressive left eye redness, pain, and photophobia that developed 2 days after completing a 28-day course of miltefosine and a 14-dose course of amphotericin B for recurrent papulonodular skin lesions. Over 7 days, visual acuity in the left eye deteriorated markedly to counting fingers.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection on dolutegravir and emtricitabine-tenofovir. Prior cutaneous and visceral disease treated initially with 7 doses of liposomal amphotericin B, and retreated 1 year later with a 14-dose course of amphotericin and 28 days of miltefosine. Denied prior ocular disease. Epidemiological history: immigrated to the United States from Nicaragua at age 20 and resided in the US continuously thereafter.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports left eye redness, ocular pain, and photophobia; denies other acute systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic: nonulcerative papulonodular hypopigmented rash distributed across bilateral upper and lower extremities, trunk, and abdomen. Abdomen: splenomegaly noted. Ophthalmic examination (left eye): visual acuity reduced to counting fingers; biomicroscopy showed 3+ conjunctival and ciliary injection, peripheral corneal haze with focal areas of whitening without epithelial loss or ulceration, and 1+ anterior chamber cells; shallow temporal choroidal effusion on fundus exam; no vitreoretinal involvement.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count revealed thrombocytopenia. HIV viral load: 10,500 copies/mL; CD4 count: 213 cells/mm^3. Infectious serologies and tests: serum RPR/FTA non-reactive; QuantiFERON-TB Gold negative; serum VZV antibodies noncontributory.
objective.advanced_workup: Cutaneous biopsy: hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining showed dermal histiocytic infiltration with intracellular organisms. Anterior chamber paracentesis: performed for diagnostic PCR analysis; herpes zoster virus (HZV) aqueous PCR was negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Cutaneous biopsy H&E staining demonstrated Leishmania infantum amastigotes, confirming cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis with secondary ocular anterior uveitis/interstitial keratitis. Anterior chamber paracentesis performed for Leishmania PCR. Alternative etiologies (herpes zoster, syphilis, tuberculosis) ruled out by negative HZV aqueous PCR, serum RPR/FTA, and QuantiFERON Gold. Management and Outcome: Initiated on topical prednisolone acetate 1% every 2 hours and cyclopentolate 1% three times daily under close monitoring (with backup plan for topical amphotericin B). Rapid resolution of corneal infiltration and anterior uveitis was achieved, with visual acuity restoring to 20/20 on Snellen chart. Ocular quiescence was maintained off topical steroids for 2 years, despite subsequent recurrence of systemic cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis.
